title: Overtaking & Being Overtaken
whatItIs: Overtake only when safe and legal, give vulnerable road users at least as much room as a car, and never obstruct someone overtaking you.
keyFacts: Before overtaking: road clear ahead, nobody overtaking you, and a gap to return to.
Mirrors, signal, blind-spot glance, then move out. Pass quickly; don't cut in.

keyFacts.text: You MUST NOT overtake across double white lines with the solid line nearest you (rule 129 exceptions).
You MUST NOT overtake after a 'No Overtaking' sign, or the vehicle nearest a crossing.

keyFacts: Overtake on the left only if the vehicle ahead is signalling right and there's room.
Being overtaken: steady course and speed; if they cut in, drop back to a two-second gap.

visual.caption: Guide clearances (rule 163): if you can't give them, wait

a.label: MUST NOT overtake (165)
points: Double white lines, solid line nearest you
Into a bus, tram or cycle lane in its hours

b.label: Do not overtake (166–167)
points: Approaching a bend, hump bridge or brow
When a road user is signalling right

onTheTest.question: Your pupil is behind a cyclist on a 30 mph road. As a guide, the minimum space when overtaking is:
onTheTest.why: Rule 163: leave at least 1.5 m when overtaking cyclists at up to 30 mph, and more at higher speeds. If you can't, wait behind.

onTheTest.question: Solid double white lines on your side; a horse rider ahead at 8 mph; road clear. May you cross to pass?
onTheTest.why: Rule 129: you may cross to pass a cycle, horse or road works vehicle at 10 mph or less. Pass wide and slow (rule 215).

traps: Don't follow a vehicle that is overtaking: there may be room for only one.
A right signal that 'should have been cancelled'? Wait: don't overtake.
Cutting in after overtaking is a DT1 judgement fault.
Large vehicles: drop back to see ahead and so the driver can see you.
